title: Cap. 6 Arg. 8 Fathers reply: Prosper—grace given makes obedience; De vocat. Gent. on hidden election
pass_a_gloss: But let us hear others also. Prosper: Who doubts that free choice obeys so great an exhortation of the Caller, when in it the grace of God has generated the affection of believing and of obeying? Therefore the grace of God is not given to choice under the condition, if it obeys, but having been given it makes that it obey. The same, On the Calling of the Gentiles book 1 chapter 18: For all human beings of whatever condition and age the cause of perceiving grace is the will of God, with whom the reason of election is hidden, merits beginning from that grace which they receive without merits. This testimony is to be noted: because although this Author (whoever he was) defends that the help of grace has not been wholly withdrawn from any human beings, nevertheless he does not judge it to stand ready and be offered to all in such a way that the discrimination why this one perceived it, that one did not perceive it, is recalled to this, that this one willed to receive, that one to resist: but he reduces the cause of grace perceived to the hidden election of God; and by consequence also of grace not-received, insofar as it is a mere negation, to the hidden non-election of God. If nevertheless it is considered as a moral omission on the part of human beings resisting grace, then it is to be referred to human viciousness. But these things by the way.
pass_b_english: Hear others too. Prosper: Who doubts that free choice obeys so great a call from the Caller, when in that choice God’s grace has already generated the affection of believing and obeying? So God’s grace is not given to the will on condition that it obey; once given, it makes the will obey. The same writer, On the Calling of the Gentiles 1.18: for people of every condition and age, the cause of receiving grace is God’s will, with whom the reason of election is hidden—merits begin from that grace which they receive without merits. Note the witness. Even if this author (whoever he was) holds that helps of grace have not been wholly withdrawn from anyone, he still does not think grace stands ready and offered to all in such a way that the difference—why this person received it and that one did not—is traced to one willing to take and the other willing to resist. He reduces the cause of grace received to God’s hidden election; and, as far as non-reception is a mere negation, he reduces that too to hidden non-election. If you treat it as a moral omission by people who resist grace, then refer it to human viciousness. But that is by the way.
source_text: Sed alios etiam audiamus. Prosper: Quis ambigat liberum arbitrium tantae cohortationi vocantis obedire, cum in illo gratia Dei affectum credendi obediendique generavit? Gratia igitur Dei non datur arbitrio sub conditione, si obediat, sed data facit ut obediat. Idem, De vocat. Gent. l. 1. c. 18. Omnibus hominibus cujuslibet conditionis et aetatis causa percipiendae gratiae voluntas Dei est, apud quem ratio electionis abscondita est, ab ea gratia incipientibus meritis quam accipere sine meritis. Notandum est hoc testimonium: quia licet hic Autor (quicunque fuerit) nullis hominibus opem gratiae in totum fuisse subtractam defendit, tamen non ita praestare et offerri omnibus arbitratur, ut discrimen, cur hic eam perceperit, ille non perceperit, eo revocetur, quod hic voluerit accipere, ille resistere: sed reducit causam gratiae perceptae ad absconditam electionem Dei; et per consequens etiam non-receptae, quatenus est mera negatio, ad absconditam non-electionem Dei. Si tamen consideretur ut moralis omissio ex parte hominum gratiae resistentium, tum referendum est ad vitiositatem humanam. Sed haec obiter.
